title: Teachers in Steubenville and his uncle's music school
summary: Howard credits two brothers in Steubenville and an uncle Howard who taught music; he cannot recall names.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What about any other teachers after you got to Los Angeles. (Inaudible) to be the kind of musician you are, because we have heard a lot about your approach, have achieved a lot of things, like a lot of the other players hadn't and a person who could read solo, could write. Where did you get into all this, was this just from you or did you meet people who inspired this?
I can't think of the name, there are two brothers. I can't think of their names. I have been trying to think of them. They were very good and they taught me to play a whole lot.
They were in Los Angeles when you came to Los Angeles?
They taught you a lot before you came to Los Angeles, but you can't remember their names.

No, I can't remember their names. They had such a funny name. But they were very good. And oh, I want to tell you this: the people I went around with, they had a meat -- not a meat place, but, Buddy, they had a business where they taught you music, something like a music school and I had an uncle --
You had an uncle who also taught music?
Was he a playing musician? Did he play in bands.
Do you know the name of the bands?
I don't know the names of the bands, but it was just like you go to a place out in the woods somewhere and play. Perhaps if I can -- maybe I'll run across it in my mind afterward. I'll try to.
